summary: Steel tower first built in 1934 at Olanta, SC; bought at auction and moved to Moore Farms Botanical Garden in 2004; now a garden landmark; NHLR-registered 2014.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a bright red top

staffing.status: no longer used for fire spotting; no lookouts named in the sources read

access.note: Garden is not open to the public every day. Visits are by request, through guided tours, open garden days and seasonal events; the garden asks visitors to book.

visit.trail_note: Book a visit through the garden. None of the sources says the tower itself can be climbed.

corrections.proposed: 1934 built at Olanta; 2004 relocated to the garden
corrections.why: The tower was originally built in 1934 at Olanta and moved to the garden in 2004. The NHLR Built field reads 2004, but its own description gives 1934.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's Built field says 2004, but its description and the garden's page say the tower dates from 1934 at Olanta and moved in 2004. The story uses 1934 for the build and 2004 for the move.
The garden's page says standing more than 100 feet tall; Wikipedia gives 100 ft (30 m). The record uses 30 m, which is Wikipedia's figure.

notes_for_editor: Ownership is described as the garden (NHLR says Moore Farms Botanical Garden, LLC). The NHLR describes the purchase as coming from the state forestry commission, while the garden and Wikipedia describe an auction in Olanta; these are compatible and the story reports both. Visit rules come from Wikipedia and the garden's booking prompt; no source says the tower can be climbed, so none is claimed. No photo credits were recorded because no image URLs were captured.
